subject: Unexpected minimums on interleaved streaming -> prefix affinity / decommit impact
messages:
From: Alex Park <alex.park@novusretail.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@novusretail.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Billing for recent pilot — saw minimums applied unexpectedly

Hi Dylan,

We ran the last week of the pilot and noticed a couple of line items on the invoice that don’t match our expectations. Specifically, we saw charges for three "minimum charge" occurrences even though the total token volume was low — looks tied to a couple of interleaved streaming calls when agents switched models mid-conversation.

Can you explain why the minimums triggered? Our engineering team (copied below) suspects it might be related to session decommit behavior whenever the model variant changes and the prefix affinity is lost. If this is expected behavior we need to understand whether that will scale to production.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Park
Head of Automation, Novus Retail

Attachments: novus_prefix-usage-sample.csv
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Alex Park <alex.park@novusretail.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@novusretail.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Billing for recent pilot — saw minimums applied unexpectedly

Hi Alex — thanks for the sample and flagging this. I dug into the calls and can confirm three short-lived streams where the request sequence switched from model A (cost-optimized) -> model B (high-accuracy) mid-session. Because our metering currently attributes a minimum to every "active inference allocation" when there is a decommit (the worker is torn down and later restarted on a different variant), the system counted those as separate billable units which triggered the minimums.

Quick summary of what's happening:
- Interleaved streaming + model switch -> prefix/kv affinity lost.
- Decommit creates a short allocation that falls below the per-call minimum quantum.
- Billing logic currently floors those to the configured minimums rather than aggregating them across the session boundary.

We should have a fix in the pipeline to do fast-session rehydration for affinity-preserving switches (reduces decommit windows) but that’s a few sprints out. For now, I want to propose either:
1) A one-off credit for the pilot minimums (recommended), or
2) A short-term config change: increase the intra-session aggregation window so micro-decommits within X seconds are stitched together for billing.

Ben — tagging you for pricing guidance and whether we can roll pilot credits. Alex — I’ll include a sample of the underlying call traces in a follow-up.

—Dylan
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Alex Park <alex.park@novusretail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jun 2025 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Billing for recent pilot — saw minimums applied unexpectedly

Alex / Dylan — I reviewed the invoice and the usage blob Dylan pointed to. Two quick thoughts:

1) Concession: For pilots under 3 months we typically grant a one-time credit equal to the sum of triggered minimums if the behavior is an artifact of product immaturity (which this looks like). I can approve up to a $3k credit from Sales Operations; anything beyond requires finance sign-off.

2) Longer-term: We can offer Novus a deployment knob for aggregation window (default 30s) to stitch micro allocations for Dedicated customers. That is policy/config work but doable; would require agreement on what happens under sustained burst vs heartbeat scenarios.

Dylan — please confirm the aggregated minimums value we expect from Alex’s CSV and I’ll queue the pilot credit. Karthik — FYI on the technical knob if we want to bake into Redwood Dedicated config.

-Ben
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Park <alex.park@novusretail.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jun 2025 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Billing for recent pilot — saw minimums applied unexpectedly

Ben / Dylan / Alex — quick technical note on options and impact:

- Prefix affinity: preserving KV/prefix across in-memory switching reduces cold-start decommit frequency and therefore reduces occurrences of minimum-quantum charges. This requires affinity-preserving routing and small changes to our cache pinning logic.
- Aggregation window: increasing from 30s -> 90s stitches more micro allocations but raises risk of charging a single long-running session under sustained multi-variant bursts; we can mitigate by counting token throughput rather than wall-clock and only stitch if total tokens < threshold.
- Temporary workaround: if Novus can pin to a single model family for higher frequency flows, that will avoid decommit churn.

Action items we agreed on in-thread:
- Dylan: run the CSV through the billing simulator and send an itemized delta (expected credit).
- Ben: pre-approve up to $3k pilot credit; hold finance escalation for anything higher.
- Karthik: scope the config change and estimate implementation effort (ETA: 3 sprints for conservative rollout).

Alex — apologies for the confusion. We’ll follow up with a formal credit note and a short doc on recommended routing/pinning patterns for production.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Product, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-credit-term.docx
